dublinCore.title: Möbius Transform
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Möbius transformations
Conformal mapping
Complex functions
Bilinear transform
IIR filter design
dublinCore.description: Interactive explorer for the Möbius transformation w = (Az + B)/(Cz + D). A grid of points in the input z-plane and its image in the output w-plane are drawn at the same scale; draggable coefficient vectors, presets (identity, rotation, inversion, bilinear, Cayley), freehand drawing that is mapped through f, and read-outs of AD - BC, the pole -D/C and f(infinity) = A/C.
relation: Chapter 10: Advanced Filter Design and Implementation

topic: Poles and the point at infinity
learningObjectives: Calculate the pole -D/C, the image of infinity A/C and the determinant AD - BC of a Möbius transformation from its coefficients
Predict whether a line or circle in the z-plane maps to a line or a circle, from its position relative to the pole
Explain how B translates the plane, A rotates and scales it, and a nonzero C bends lines into circles
Demonstrate that the bilinear map (1+s)/(1-s) sends the imaginary axis onto the unit circle and the left half-plane inside it
Calculate the warped digital frequency omega = 2 arctan(Omega) of a point s = j Omega under the bilinear map with T = 2
prerequisites: Complex arithmetic in rectangular and polar form
Stability regions in the s-plane and z-plane

misconceptions.misconception: A Möbius transformation keeps straight lines straight
misconceptions.correction: Lines and circles map to lines and circles; a line stays a line only if it passes through the pole -D/C
misconceptions.evidence: With the Inversion preset and Scale 2, trace the line Re z = 1: its image is the circle |w - 0.5| = 0.5; the real axis, which passes through the pole at 0, stays straight

misconceptions.misconception: The bilinear transform maps analog frequency evenly onto the unit circle
misconceptions.correction: omega = 2 arctan(Omega T / 2) compresses high analog frequencies toward z = -1 (frequency warping)
misconceptions.evidence: With the Bilinear preset, Omega from 0 to 1 covers 90 degrees of the circle, 1 to 3 about 53 degrees, and everything above 3 the last 37 degrees; the grid dots crowd near w = -1

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Möbius transform explorer. The input z-plane on the left shows a grid of white points and the output w-plane on the right shows their images under w = (Az + B)/(Cz + D). Drag the colored dots in the Coefficients box to change A, B, C and D, choose a preset, draw in the input plane, and use the Scale and Density sliders. Read-outs give AD - BC, the pole -D/C, f(infinity) = A/C and the value of f at the pointer.

colorScheme.frames: light gray (200) with black axes and white grid points
colorScheme.coefficients: A red, B green, C blue, D black
colorScheme.highlight: gold pointer marker, red pole marker

controls.label: Scale
controls.description: Sets the half-width R of both the input and output plots, which show -R to R on each axis

controls.label: Density
controls.description: Sets the number of grid points per row and column in the input plane (density x density points)

controls.label: Preset
controls.description: Loads exact coefficients A, B, C, D; switches to Custom when a coefficient dot is dragged

controls.label: Clear drawing
controls.description: Erases the freehand drawing in the input plane and its image in the output plane

visualElements.description: Input z-plane: grid of white points, unit circle, red pole marker at -D/C, the user's purple drawing and a gold pointer marker; drag inside it to draw
Output w-plane: images of the grid points and of the drawing, unit circle, black ring at f(infinity) = A/C and the image of the pointer
Coefficients box: A, B, C and D as draggable colored vectors in the square |Re|, |Im| <= 1, values rounded to 0.01
The formula, the coefficient values, AD - BC (with a warning when it is zero), the pole, f(infinity), and z and f(z) at the pointer

model.description: Evaluates the Möbius transformation w = (Az + B)/(Cz + D) with complex arithmetic on a grid of input points and on the user's drawing (subdivided so its image follows the true curved path)

instructionalStrategies: Trace lines and circles and identify their images
Change one coefficient at a time
extensions: Add a pre-warping control that shows where an analog cutoff frequency lands on the unit circle
Color the grid points by half-plane to follow regions through the map
